# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently
# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

content.text:
I've written the acceptance tests for the change request.

## What the change is

> "I call these jobs, not projects. Please use that word everywhere."

This is a **user-visible terminology rename** (project → job). Crucially:
- `data-testid` anchors are immutable public API and are *not* user-visible, so they keep their existing `project-*` / `nav-projects` names.
- Seeded data (client names, job names) is unchanged.

So the change touches only the static labels, headings, button text, column headers, empty-state copy, and the search placeholder. I confirmed by reading the frontend that the word surfaces in exactly these anchored places and nowhere else hidden.

## What I did

**Added one spec:** `e2e/specs/jobs-terminology.spec.ts` (9 tests), each scoped to a `data-testid` element and asserting it now carries the new word and no longer the old one (old matched with `/project/i` to catch both "Project" and "project"; seeded names chosen to contain neither "project" nor "job" so assertions can't pass/fail by accident). Surfaces covered:

| Surface | Anchor | before → after |
|---|---|---|
| Nav link | `nav-projects` | "Projects" → "Jobs" |
| Jobs list page | `projects-page`, `project-form-submit` | "Projects" heading, "Add project" |
| Empty list | `projects-empty` | "No projects yet." |
| Job detail | `project-detail-page` | "Project" heading |
| Client page | `client-counts`, `client-projects-show-all` | "Projects" label, "Show all projects" |
| Client empty | `client-projects-empty` | "No projects for this client yet." |
| Dashboard | `dashboard` | "Projects" figure label |
| Global search | `global-search` placeholder, `search-projects` | "Search clients and projects", "Project" column |
| All invoices | `all-invoices-table` | "Project" column header |

**No existing specs changed:** I grepped the 51 existing specs — none assert these static labels (they assert via testids + seeded values), so the rename revises no behaviour they cover and they stay valid.

## Verification

- All **9 new tests fail against the pre-change app** for the right reason (e.g. the invoices table reads `ProjectAmountStage…` with no "job") — exactly the expected "should fail before the change" state.
- I did **not** modify any application code, build script, or support helper.

One thing to flag honestly: the full-suite run showed **18 existing specs already failing** against this pre-change checkpoint (line-items, payments, notes ordering, tags, budget, invoice totals). I verified two of them fail **in isolation**, so these are pre-existing checkpoint failures unrelated to this terminology change and not introduced by my spec — the rename neither affects nor fixes them.
